enunciado: Pierre de Coubertin, fundador dos Jogos Olímpicos modernos, ganhou uma medalha de ouro olímpica em 1912. Em quê?
explicacao: Os Jogos de Estocolmo de 1912 tiveram concursos de arte com medalhas. O ouro de literatura foi para a «Ode ao Desporto», assinada por Georges Hohrod e M. Eschbach, dados como alemães. Era um duplo pseudónimo: o autor do poema era o próprio Coubertin.

fontes.excerto: The gold medal for literature was awarded to “Georges Hohrod et M. Eschbach, Germany”, for the work “Ode to Sport,” [...] But in reality, the poetic ode had been written by Pierre, Baron de Coubertin, who entered it in the competitions under the dual pseudonym.

fontes.titulo: Smithsonian Magazine – Poetry Was an Official Olympic Event for Nearly 40 Years. What Happened?
fontes.excerto: they were pseudonyms for the man who had conceived the whole idea: The author of “Ode to Sport” was none other than Coubertin himself. [...] Organizers put the arts competitions on hold until the Stockholm Games in 1912.
